primary_source.authors: T. Juskevicius and J. D. Lee
primary_source.title: Small ball probabilities, maximum density and rearrangements
primary_source.result_used: Theorem 1 and the one-dimensional Rogozin maximum-density consequence

partner_result.application: Replaced generic bank caps by sharp Rogozin coefficient-sensitive caps in the partner three-bank inequality.

mathematical_change.statement: For an exact disjoint physical three-bank factorization with invertible compressed B, defining R(u) as the maximum density of the convolution of centered uniforms of widths |u_i| gives ||p_Q||_infinity <= (2*pi+3*sqrt(3))/sigma_min(D_R^{-1} B D_R^{-1}), with continuous density.
mathematical_change.concrete_bound: Three equal triple-coordinate banks give (27/16)(2*pi+3sqrt(3))/sigma_min(B)=19.37138241918299.../sigma_min(B), improving the coarse partner payment by 15.625%.

unresolved_implication: Outside the ridge/spectral-window branch, derive from only the three-large-eigenvalue hypothesis a product-preserving compression with uniformly positive weighted bank score sigma_min(D_R^{-1}BD_R^{-1}) while controlling non-bank remainder interactions, or prove a source-valid stability theorem replacing exact factorization.
next_step: Use sharp bank-cap geometry together with high-leverage decomposition and the newest one-sided cross-aggregate branch; do not return to refuted local-minor, single-Schur, post-rotation-independence, or absolute-Fourier mechanisms.
